title: School completion, Northern Africa and Western Asia, by wealth
headline: In N. Africa and W. Asia, primary completion for all by 2030 needs the rate to rise 1.7 points a year
subtitle: Percentage of a cohort of children or young people aged 3-5 years above the intended age for the last grade of primary education who have completed primary education
years: So far it has risen 0.7 points a year, from 74.4% in 2000 to 90.0% in 2024.
data_line: Data: UNESCO UIS via UN SDG Global Database, series SE_TOT_CPLR, extracted 1 Nov 2026
alt: In N. Africa and W. Asia, primary completion for all by 2030 needs the rate to rise 1.7 points a year. So far it has risen 0.7 points a year, from 74.4% in 2000 to 90.0% in 2024. Children completing primary school, Northern Africa and Western Asia: 74.4% in 2000, 90.0% in 2024. At that pace about 93.9% in 2030; reaching 100% needs 1.7 points a year.
method: Method: linear pace, 2000 to 2024; target year 2030.
question: Where has primary completion moved at anything like 1.7 points a year, and what made it possible?
